title: ASADI: Accelerating Sparse Attention Using Diagonal-based In-Situ Computing
problem: Self-attention is the performance bottleneck in Transformers for long sequences, and sparse attention introduces significant random access overhead that limits computational efficiency. Sparse attention lacks strong row/column locality but exhibits excellent diagonal locality, which existing sparse matrix paradigms fail to exploit efficiently.
motivation: Self-attention is the performance bottleneck of Transformer-based language models, particularly for long sequences, making acceleration critical.
method: ASADI employs a software-hardware co-design. The software proposes a new sparse matrix computation paradigm that directly supports diagonal (DIA) format for self-attention, exploiting the natural diagonal locality. The hardware presents a novel sparse attention accelerator using highly parallel in-situ computing to efficiently implement this computation paradigm.
key_novelty: Exploiting diagonal locality in sparse attention through a DIA-format-optimized sparse matrix computation paradigm paired with in-situ accelerator hardware.
contributions: Software-hardware co-designed sparse attention accelerator (ASADI) architecture
Novel sparse matrix computation paradigm with direct DIA format support for attention
In-situ computing hardware accelerator efficiently implementing diagonal-based computation
Experimental validation across models showing 18.6× speedup and 2.9× energy savings
limitations: Hardware implementation details and scalability limits not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: sparse attention acceleration via diagonal compression
